prompt: Before fitting a volatility model, you regress squared residuals on their own lags and test whether all the lag coefficients are zero.
tells: regress squared residuals on their own lags
whether all the lag coefficients are zero
trap: Clustering is the property; this is the test for it.

prompt: After fitting GARCH(1,1), you run Ljung–Box on the squared standardized residuals and find no remaining autocorrelation.
why: Diagnostics on squared standardized residuals check that the variance dynamics were captured.
trap: Plain residuals check the mean; squared standardized ones check the variance.

prompt: The ARCH-LM test on a monthly series gives p = 0.62. A teammate still wants to fit GARCH.
why: No evidence of ARCH effects; a constant-variance model may be enough.
trap: The test result is the deciding fact here.

prompt: After fitting an ARCH(1), the ARCH-LM test on standardized residuals is still significant at lag 5.
why: Leftover ARCH means the variance model is too short; GARCH(1,1) usually captures long memory compactly.
trap: The test tells you the model is inadequate; the remedy is a richer variance model.

prompt: Ljung–Box on raw residuals passes, but Ljung–Box on their squares fails badly.
why: Mean is fine, variance isn't: conditional heteroskedasticity is present.
trap: Read which version of the test failed.

prompt: A diagnostic regresses squared standardized residuals on an indicator for past negative shocks to see if a symmetric GARCH missed something.
why: The Engle–Ng sign bias test checks for unmodeled asymmetry.
trap: A significant result would point to GJR or EGARCH, but this step is the test.
